summary.intent: Replace the rough remote Web UI with a UI that is consistent with the desktop app.
repo_evidence: Current remote UI is hand-built in apps/desktop/layer/renderer/src/remote/remote-app.tsx with custom header, pills, panels, and raw form controls.
Desktop UI has reusable layout/component surfaces in modules/app-layout, modules/subscription-column, modules/entry-column, modules/entry-content, modules/settings.
Remote runtime and main-process application services are already available from the prior full-web-client build.
confirmed: User selected option A: strong UI consistency. Web should reuse/closely mirror the desktop main reader framework and component shape: subscription column, entry list, reading pane, visual tokens, empty states, list items, reader content, and desktop-like settings/modal styling while hiding unsupported browser-native controls.

User confirmed first-pass non-goals: no window controls, tray, dock badge, open-at-login, system notifications, system fonts, native folder picker, system proxy, Electron menu/command palette/shortcut parity, desktop integration entrypoints, AI/translation/summary online surfaces, player/corner media window.

User selected desktop-like modal/drawer placement for management capabilities: the first screen should be a desktop-like three-pane reader, while subscription management, batch operations, settings/RSSHub, import/export, and similar management workflows should live in polished desktop-style modals or drawers.

User confirmed controlled browser degradations: Web parity means desktop-like visual/read workflow parity, not 1:1 replication of every Electron-native interaction. Browser download may replace native save dialog; native folder picker remains hidden; command palette/shortcuts are not first-pass acceptance; settings expose Web-safe groups only; toolbar/action menus may replace hard-to-reuse context menus; mobile may be responsive folded parity.
User selected success-criteria option B: desktop/wide-browser screenshot verification is required; mobile responsive support is desirable but not a hard screenshot gate for the first pass.
summary.pressure_pass: Confirmed that strong desktop UI consistency allows browser-appropriate degradation and does not require copying every Electron-native behavior.
success_criteria: First screen is desktop-like three-pane reader: subscription/category column, entry list, reading pane.
Use existing desktop design tokens/component style: typography, spacing, borders, hover, selected, empty and loading states.
No raw full-screen management form panels; management workflows use desktop-style modal/drawer surfaces.
Subscription management, batch management, settings/RSSHub, and import/export are accessible without polluting the main reading layout.
Entry list, reading content, toolbar/actions, connection state, refresh state, empty states, and error states look production-quality and consistent with desktop.
Verification must include at least one desktop/wide-browser screenshot; mobile screenshot is not a first-pass hard gate.
